mainTopic: Is it allowed to have the first relations with a בתולה on שבת? The dispute between רב and שמואל, and how it connects to ר' שמעון's rule about an unintended forbidden result (דבר שאין מתכוון) and the exception of פסיק רישיה.
overview: This page opens with the last words of a question from the previous page: in the case of first relations with a בתולה on שבת, does the הלכה follow ר' יהודה, who forbids an act with an unintended forbidden result, or ר' שמעון, who permits it? The גמרא quotes two opposite reports of a dispute between רב and שמואל. רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory aid: each city calls its own teacher the lenient one. The גמרא challenges the report that רב permits, since רב forbids pushing a cloth stopper tightly into a barrel on יום טוב. It answers that the barrel case is a פסיק רישיה, a certain result, which even ר' שמעון forbids. A second challenge points out that רב rules like ר' יהודה in general. The answer is that רב does follow ר' יהודה, but first relations are a destructive act (מקלקל) under either understanding of the blood, so they are permitted anyway. Finally רב חסדא quotes a משנה in נדה about the nights given to a bride, ending at מוצאי שבת, to build a new challenge that continues on the next page.

steps.title: Finishing the question: do we follow רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: These words close the question begun on the previous page: in the case of first relations with a בתולה on שבת, does the הלכה follow ר' שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: Or is the הלכה like ר' שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a question that started on the previous page. It asks whether we follow ר' יהודה or ר' שמעון here, and it sets up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about first relations with a בתולה on שבת, where blood comes out along with the act. The two sides are ר' יהודה (the stricter view) and ר' שמעון. The following steps show that the issue is a forbidden result that the person does not intend.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who is lenient about a forbidden result that is not intended (דבר שאין מתכוון)

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not stand alone. The word או ("or") shows it is the second half of a question that began on the previous daf.

phrases.english: Or is the law like Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: This is the second half of a question; the first half, about following ר' יהודה, was on the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question from the previous page.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the practical הלכה follows ר' שמעון's lenient view in the case of first relations on שבת.

steps.title: Two opposite reports of the dispute between רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב's school reports that רב permits and שמואל forbids. In נהרדעא they report the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: In רב's study hall they say that רב permits and שמואל forbids. In נהרדעא they say that רב forbids and שמואל permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between רב and שמואל about our question. Two places report the dispute in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports agree that there is a dispute. They disagree about who holds which view. The one who permits seems to follow ר' שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated; introduces a dispute among אמוראים

phrases.english: (It was stated:) In the house of Rav they say:
phrases.notes: Some versions do not have the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: Rav permits and Shmuel forbids.
In Neharde'a they say:
Rav forbids and Shmuel permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an אמוראים dispute that bears on the question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב and שמואל disagree about first relations on שבת, but the reports conflict on who permits.

steps.title: A memory aid: each city calls its own teacher lenient
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a way to remember the two reports: each place reports that its own teacher holds the lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Your memory aid is that these are lenient for themselves and those are lenient for themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a simple trick to remember who said what in each report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's students say that רב permits, and שמואל's city says that שמואל permits. Each place puts the lenient view on its own local teacher, whose ruling they follow.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's school says רב permits; נהרדעא says שמואל permits. Each side reports its own teacher as the lenient one.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said,
And your memory aid is:
These are lenient for themselves,
and those are lenient for themselves.
phrases.notes: Each group reports that its own local teacher holds the lenient view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a way to remember the two opposite reports.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each place attributes the lenient view to its own teacher.

steps.title: Challenge: רב forbids pushing a cloth stopper into a barrel
steps.stepSummary: How can רב permit? רב said it is forbidden to push a cloth stopper tightly into a barrel on יום טוב, because liquid gets squeezed out even though no one wants it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really permit? But רב שימי בר חזקיה said in רב's name: it is forbidden to push this cloth stopper tightly into a barrel on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the report that רב permits. It quotes a different ruling of רב that sounds strict about an unintended result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you push a wet cloth stopper in tightly, liquid is squeezed out, which is forbidden, even though you do not intend it. If רב forbids that, he seems to reject ר' שמעון's leniency. Then how could he permit first relations on שבת, where the blood is also not the goal?

phrases.english: And does Rav permit?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִזְקִיָּה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Shimi bar Chizkiyah say in the name of Rav:
This cloth stopper of a barrel,
it is forbidden to push it in tightly on a Festival!
phrases.notes: Pushing it in squeezes liquid out of the cloth, and that is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שָׁרֵי? וְהָאָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִזְקִיָּה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the report from רב's school that רב permits.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רב permits first relations on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב forbids an act with an unintended forbidden result (squeezing), so he should also forbid relations, where the blood is not the goal.

steps.title: Answer: an unavoidable result is forbidden even for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: In the barrel case the squeezing is certain to happen, which makes it a פסיק רישיה. אביי and רבא both say that even ר' שמעון forbids such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case even ר' שמעון agrees, because אביי and רבא both say: ר' שמעון agrees in a case of "cut off its head and won't it die?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the barrel case is different, so רב can still permit in our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ר' שמעון permits an unintended result only when it might not happen. When the result is certain, like death after cutting off a head, even he forbids it. The squeezing is certain, so רב's ruling on the barrel does not contradict a lenient ruling that follows ר' שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: "Cut off its head and won't it die?"; a result that is certain to happen

steps.whatToRemember: ר' שמעון's leniency for an unintended result does not apply when the result is unavoidable (פסיק רישיה).
steps.whyThisMatters: פסיק רישיה is a basic rule throughout הלכות שבת: an unintended result is still forbidden when it is certain to happen.
steps.confusionAlert: פסיק רישיה does not mean the person wants the result. He does not intend it, but it is certain to happen, so ר' שמעון's leniency does not apply.

phrases.english: In that case even Rabbi Shimon agrees,
for Abaye and Rava both say:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of "cut off its head and won't it die?"
phrases.notes: This is a picture of something certain: if you cut off an animal's head, of course it dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by setting the barrel case apart.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the barrel case is an unavoidable result.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's barrel ruling shows he rejects ר' שמעון's leniency entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel case is a פסיק רישיה, forbidden even for ר' שמעון, so רב can still follow ר' שמעון and permit in our case.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יהודה, so how can he permit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings reports that רב rules like רבי יהודה and שמואל rules like רבי שמעון. That makes it hard to say רב is the one who permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חייא בר אשי say in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה? And רב חנן בר אמי said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. And רב חייא בר אבין teaches it without the names in between: רב said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the report from רב's school that רב permits. It points out that רב is on record ruling like רבי יהודה, the stricter opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין, an act whose forbidden result you don't intend. רבי שמעון permits it. If רב rules like רבי יהודה, he should forbid first relations on שבת, so the report that he permits looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An act where the forbidden result is not intended
The final law follows this opinion
Without the men; quoting the ruling without the chain of names

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chiyya bar Ashi say in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: This is about an act whose forbidden result you don't intend. רבי יהודה forbids it.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And Rav Chanan bar Ami said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּלָא גַּבְרֵי,
phrases.english: And Rav Chiyya bar Avin teaches it without the men,
phrases.notes: He gives the same rulings straight from רב and שמואל, without naming the people who passed them on.

phrases.english: Rav said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the barrel case, the גמרא raises a second challenge to רב permitting.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report from רב's school that רב permits first relations on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules like רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין, so רב should forbid this act too.

steps.title: רב follows רבי יהודה, but this act is destructive
steps.stepSummary: רב does hold like רבי יהודה. But first relations are a destructive act (מקלקל), whichever way we understand the blood, so they are not forbidden even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, רב holds like רבי יהודה. According to the version that says the blood is stored, he is destroying in making the opening. According to the version that says the blood is attached, he is destroying in making the wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב can rule like רבי יהודה and still permit. The reason is that this particular act counts as destructive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a destructive act (מקלקל) is not the kind of forbidden work the תורה means. The two versions from earlier argue about what the problem is: making an opening if the blood is stored, or wounding if the blood is attached. Either way, the act is destructive, so even רבי יהודה would not forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who damages or destroys; not a real forbidden work on שבת
The blood is stored, collected in one place
The blood is attached, flowing in the body's vessels

steps.whatToRemember: רב rules like רבי יהודה, but first relations on שבת are still allowed because the act is מקלקל, destructive.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב switched to רבי שמעון's side. He stays with רבי יהודה. The היתר comes from the act being destructive, not from it being unintended.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם רַב כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Really, Rav holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
according to that version which says
the blood is stored,
he is destroying with regard to the opening.
phrases.notes: In this version the concern was making an opening. Here that opening is made in a damaging way.

phrases.english: According to that version which says
the blood is attached,
he is destroying by making the wound.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַב כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise but shows it does not apply here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב follows רבי יהודה, he must forbid this unintended act.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי יהודה does not forbid this act, because it is destructive under either understanding of the blood.

steps.title: רב חסדא quotes a משנה about how many nights a bride is given
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא opens an objection from a משנה in נדה. The משנה tells us how long blood after the wedding is blamed on the wound rather than counted as נדה blood. בית הלל say "until מוצאי שבת, four nights."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: A young girl whose time to see blood has not yet come, and she married: בית שמאי say we give her four nights, and בית הלל say until the wound heals. If her time to see blood has come, and she married: בית שמאי say we give her the first night, and בית הלל say until מוצאי שבת, four nights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא quotes a משנה to set up a challenge. In this step the גמרא only brings the source; the actual question comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the bride time during which any blood is blamed on the wound, so she stays permitted to her husband. In the second case, בית הלל count four nights ending at מוצאי שבת, and that count includes Friday night. Pay attention to this, because רב חסדא seems to be building a challenge from it to the opinion that forbids first relations on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection from a source
She has reached the age when she would see menstrual blood

phrases.english: Rav Chisda raised an objection:
A young girl whose time to see blood has not arrived
and she married,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹתְנִין לָהּ אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: We give her four nights,
phrases.notes: During these nights any blood is blamed on the wound, so she stays permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁתִּחְיֶה הַמַּכָּה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: Until the wound heals.
If her time to see blood has arrived and she married,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: We give her the first night.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת, אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת.
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: Until Saturday night, four nights.
phrases.notes: A בתולה married on Wednesday, so counting from Wednesday night, the four nights end at Saturday night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב, the גמרא opens a new challenge from a משנה about the wedding nights.
steps.kashyaTarget: Seemingly the view that forbids first relations on שבת (the question continues on the next page)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית הלל's four nights run until מוצאי שבת and include Friday night. This seems to assume first relations may happen even on שבת.
